analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. The date is bumped to 2026-10-14, and head lines 129-153 add "Unregistered GLM sparse-state candidate". The new text describes GLM5NextPagedSparseState, PagedImmutableSnapshot copy-on-write, and a distinct full-state codec layout, `native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1`. It states that SSD prefix-cache eligibility defaults on for the locally selected `EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp` via `PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel`, and that `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` opts out. It also says GLM is outside the coordinator's registered serving models. No code, protocol or config change is in the supplied evidence, so no security control is visibly altered. The base-text units (lines 443-856) are unchanged context.

Relevant threat IDs: T-041 and SEC-035 (cross-tenant TTFT oracle and at-rest SSD artifacts), A-001, TB-007.

Open question for the next pass: T-041 and its detection_hint treat the default-on SSD gate as an enumerated, signed-off surface. Adding GLM to the default-on set could widen the at-rest and timing surface (new full-state, recurrent and MTP payload). The supplied evidence does not show the code that implements `isGLM5NextDefaultModel`. It also does not show whether the HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping, 30-minute TTL and KEK binding apply to the new store. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.

A reviewer with the actual PrefixCachePolicy+Activation.swift and GLM codec diff should confirm those controls. They should also decide whether T-041 needs a note about the GLM default-on scope. The doc says GLM is unregistered with the coordinator, so the coordinator-authored cacheSalt may not apply on that path.
